chunks.content: 96 Want to Make a Seller Hate You? Put This in Your LOI Hi Sara, Let’s play a game. What’s one thing you can put in your Letter of Intent that instantly makes a seller question your ability to run anything, much less their business? Answer: A 0% interest seller note. Yikes. I see this all the time. Some eager buyer (probably fresh off a YouTube binge) sends in an LOI offering seller financing at 0% interest—as if that’s a totally normal, savvy move. Spoiler: it’s not usually. Here’s why that “interest-free” offer makes sellers cringe (and quietly blacklist you): It’s a tax trap. Even if the seller agrees to 0%, the IRS doesn’t. Imputed interest means the seller still pays taxes as if they earned interest. So you're not just offering a bad deal—you're offering one that costs them. It signals you don’t understand deals. Or at least, you haven't Googled “applicable federal rate.” Offering a loan below that rate without understanding the tax consequences doesn’t scream "trustworthy operator of a tax firm." It kills motivation to repay. Would you rush to pay off an interest-free loan? Neither would your seller. That’s why they’re unlikely to love the idea of giving you one. It’s not 2010. Inflation is real. Cost of capital is real. And unless your seller is feeling wildly philanthropic, they need a very good reason why they should finance your dream at 0%. The fix? At a minimum, offer AFR (Applicable Federal Rate) on seller notes. Show the seller that you understand basic finance, tax implications, and how not to look like a rookie. Not sure what AFR is or how to structure a seller note that doesn't make you look like a walking red flag? You can watch one of my recent videos right here. I’ll walk you through it, no fluff.
